note: Every figure below was read from the named source during this session unless it sits in `uncertain`. Derived shares are marked `derived: true` and show their arithmetic.

validPassportsInCirculation.unit: valid US passport documents (books + cards), end of fiscal year
validPassportsInCirculation.source: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/about-us/reports-and-statistics.html (table 'Valid Passports in Circulation by Fiscal Year (1989-2025)'; read from the Wayback copy of 2026-07-12 because the live page returns 403 to automated fetches)
validPassportsInCirculation.caveat: State's own note: 'a customer who has both a passport book and card has two valid passports. Some customers may also have two valid passport books.' So this counts documents, not people. State publishes no count of distinct holders.

passportsIssuedFY2025.unit: passports issued in FY2025 (includes 4,544,022 passport cards)

documentsPerResident.unit: valid passport documents per US resident
documentsPerResident.source: derived from the two rows above
documentsPerResident.caveat: An upper bound on the share of residents holding a passport, not the share: book+card holders count twice, and the denominator includes non-citizens (who cannot hold a US passport). No official count of distinct holders or of citizens-with-passport was found.

licensedDrivers20to24.unit: licensed drivers aged 20-24 (male 9,234,136; female 8,631,909; the total exceeds their sum by 15,459, presumably drivers with sex not reported)
licensedDrivers20to24.source: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/statistics/2024/dl20.cfm (Highway Statistics 2024, Table DL-20, 'Licensed Drivers: Distribution by Sex and Age Group Relative to Population')

percentOfAgeGroupLicensed.unit: percent of population aged 20-24 holding a driver's licence (as stated by FHWA)

populationUsedByFHWA.source: FHWA footnote names the denominator as Census SC-EST2024-AGESEX-CIV; summed from https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2024/state/asrh/sc-est2024-agesex-civ.csv (United States, SEX=0, AGE 20-24, POPEST2024_CIV)

ukPassportHolders.unit: million usual residents (76.7%) holding a UK passport

englandAndWales.scope: England and Wales only; ONS does not cover Scotland (Census 2022, NRS) or Northern Ireland (Census 2021, NISRA). Dataset tables: TS005 https://www.ons.gov.uk/datasets/TS005/editions/2021

validPassportsInCirculation.unit: million, stated as 'over 27 million passports in circulation'
validPassportsInCirculation.statedDate: no as-at date given; page modified 2026-09-04 (same wording in the May 2025 minister binder, modified 2025-09-11)

shareHoldingValidPassport.unit: percent of all Canadians, stated as 'Approximately 67%'

canada.caveat: 27M / 41.8M = 64.6%, not 67%. IRCC's 67% presumably uses a citizen-only or older denominator; it does not say. Use IRCC's stated 67% as the official share and the 27M as a floor.

mrvFeeFVisa.unit: USD, non-petition-based nonimmigrant visa application (MRV) fee, applies to F
mrvFeeFVisa.source: Federal Register 2023-06290, 88 FR (2023-03-28), final rule effective 2023-05-30: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/03/28/2023-06290/schedule-of-fees-for-consular-services-nonimmigrant-and-special-visa-fees ; still current per State's 2026-06-09 rule (FR 2026-11513): 'The MRV fee was last updated in May 2023 and is currently set at $185'

gracePeriodAfterProgram.source: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(iv) as it read on 2026-09-01: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-01/title-8.xml?part=214&section=214.2 — 'an additional 60-day period to prepare for departure'
gracePeriodAfterProgram.status: DHS's final rule (FR 2026-14439, published 2026-07-17, effective 2026-09-15) replaced duration of status with a fixed admission (max 4 years) and cut the grace period to 30 days; eCFR now prints the 30-day text. On 2026-09-14 the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts (Presidents' Alliance et al. v. DHS, Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV) granted a nationwide preliminary injunction barring DHS from implementing it, so D/S and the 60-day period remain in place while litigation continues. Sources: https://www.presidentsalliance.org/duration-of-status-litigation/ ; https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/final-rule-establishing-a-fixed-time-period-of-admission-and-an-extension-of-stay-procedure-faq (describes the 30-day rule, updated 2026-08-31, predates the injunction).

optMonths.unit: months of practical training per degree level ('A student may be authorized 12 months of practical training, and becomes eligible for another 12 months ... when they change to a higher educational level'); must be completed within 14 months of program end
optMonths.source: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10) and (f)(10)(ii)(A)(3), eCFR current as of 2026-09-25: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/section-214.2

stemOptExtensionMonths.unit: months, STEM degree extension of post-completion OPT (up to two lifetime)

i765FeeOnline.unit: USD, Form I-765 general filing (applies to OPT), online
i765FeeOnline.source: USCIS Form G-1055 Fee Schedule, Appendix C: https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/g-1055.pdf

i765OptPremiumProcessingFee.unit: USD, optional Form I-907 for I-765 OPT / STEM OPT

i129FeeOPetition.unit: USD, Form I-129 O petition (O-1 limited to one beneficiary per petition); O-1B arts and O-1B motion picture/TV use the same fee
i129FeeOPetition.statedDate: G-1055 edition 09/09/26 (amount set by the fee rule effective 2024-04-01)

i129FeePPetition.unit: USD, Form I-129 P petition (P-1, P-2, P-3; up to 25 beneficiaries)

asylumProgramFee.appliesTo: Form I-129 including O and P petitions, paid by the petitioning employer or agent

o1MaxInitialPeriod.unit: years (petition validity 'not to exceed 3 years'); extensions in increments of up to 1 year

p3MaxInitialPeriod.unit: year ('not to exceed 1 year'); extensions in 1-year increments

mrvFeePetitionBasedVisa.unit: USD, consular visa application fee for H, L, O, P, Q, R visas (paid by the worker at the consulate after petition approval)

uncertain: US share of citizens holding a passport: State counts documents (books and cards separately), not people, and publishes no holder count. 183.2M / 341.8M = 53.6% is an upper bound per resident, not the share. Secondary sources say 45-50% of Americans hold one; no official figure confirms that.

Australia: passports.gov.au, dfat.gov.au and anao.gov.au timed out from this machine, so no figure was read from an official page. Wikipedia, citing https://www.passports.gov.au/passport-facts-2024-25, gives '15 million' Australian passports in circulation (2025) and 'about 56% of the population'. Unverified; do not use as confirmed. Australian population (ABS) was also not retrieved.
UK-wide passport share: only England and Wales (ONS) was retrieved. Scotland (NRS Census 2022) and Northern Ireland (NISRA Census 2021) figures were not.
Canada: IRCC's 'over 27 million' and '67%' carry no as-at date and do not reconcile with StatCan's 41.8M population (27/41.8 = 64.6%).
USCIS normal (non-premium) processing time for Form I-765 OPT, category (c)(3)(B): egov.uscis.gov/processing-times is behind Cloudflare and was not readable. No figure given.
Visa Integrity Fee ($250, Pub. L. 119-21, July 2025): a secondary source says State has not begun collecting it; not confirmed from travel.state.gov (403). Not included in the F-1 or O/P totals.

G-1055 (edition 09/09/26) lists an 'Additional Form I-94 Fee: Pub. L. 119-21 Fee' of $24 near the I-129 rows; the PDF layout did not make clear whether it applies to every O/P petition or only to change/extension of status requesting an I-94. Not included.
Whether O and P I-129 petitions can be filed online at a lower fee: the G-1055 layout shows an online price only for some I-129 categories; the O and P amounts above are the paper/general fees.
